virality_data.topic: Why I Replaced Auto-Layout Diagram Engines with Relative Positioning in TypeScript
virality_data.analysis: Engineers using Mermaid or Graphviz regularly struggle with erratic layout engine shifts whenever a single node is edited. Reladraw surfaced a major architectural gap in current diagram tools: developers want programmatic control over explicit relative constraints rather than unpredictable black-box auto-placement algorithms. Suman breaks down the engineering trade-offs between force-directed layouts and relative graph constraint engines.

GitHub: Declarative diagramming engines trending among frontend engineers
Dev Community: High frustration with Mermaid auto-layout regressions
virality_data.story_angle: Every time I modified a single node in our system diagram, Mermaid reshuffled the entire architecture layout, forcing me to build a constraint-based relative rendering engine in TypeScript.
